title: Day 753: Two Men Killed in Broad-Daylight Attack Outside Sinaloa Government Palace in Culiacán
detail: Around 1:00 PM on Saturday, August 15, 2026, gunmen using automatic rifles killed two unidentified men riding in a white Nissan Versa on Avenida José Aguilar Barraza near the Sinaloa State Government Palace in downtown Culiacán. The vehicle came to rest facing the wrong way near Lázaro Cárdenas and Constitución after the attack. An IMSS employee badge was found inside the car, though it was unclear if it belonged to either victim. No arrests were reported despite a heavy police, state and military presence around the Government Palace. The killing occurred the same day Infobae reported that Sinaloa was on pace for a record homicide year alongside a forensic crisis, with the Mazatlán morgue overwhelmed by unidentified remains.

title: Day 753: Sinaloa Heads for Record Homicide Year as Mazatlán Morgue Faces Forensic Crisis
detail: Infobae reported on August 15, 2026 that Sinaloa is on pace for a record homicide year, with a violence map shifting toward Mazatlán after two years concentrated in Culiacán. Culiacán historically accounted for roughly 8 of every 10 murders and disappearances in the state over the prior two years, but Mazatlán's Semefo (forensic medical service) is now saturated with unidentified bodies, hampered by a lack of budget for genetic testing. A clandestine grave with burned remains was located in Ceuta, Elota municipality, on August 14. Search collectives have protested demanding adequate forensic attention for families of the disappeared.

media.caption: Sinaloa's forensic services strain under a record homicide count, August 2026
